hold_text: check_pr_landing.py's R5 refuses self-land here: this PR edits CONTENT (not just last_dispatched_at) inside three pre-registered decision-rule queue units -- RQ-20260927-006.yaml and RQ-20260927-008.yaml (a one-word id fix inside a cross-reference sentence: RQ-20260927-005 -> RQ-20260927-009) and the renumbered RQ-20260927-009.yaml itself (id field only; its decision_rule/power/routing/blocked_on blocks are byte-identical to the file's prior content at research/queue/blocked/RQ-20260927-005.yaml, verified via `git show <old-blob>` vs the new file). The guard's rule is blanket (a pre-registered decision rule may not self-land on any content change), which is the right call in general even though this specific change is a pure id-collision fix with no effect on any decision_rule, power, or routing field. Asking for one human read rather than arguing the guard down, per this repo's own pr-landing-guard precedent (R5/R6/R10 examples in git history). Also fixes PI (files) docs/claude/work/pipeline/<new>.json (a plain pipeline finding, Tier-1, no objection) and RQ-20260927-005.yaml's id collision itself (the landed W6-PROP-R3 unit keeps the id unchanged -- not touched by this PR).
why: research/** and docs/claude/work/pipeline/** are on the Tier-1 surface: no src/, config/, scripts/, or workflow change. Renumbers one blocked (never-run) research unit to clear an id collision with a landed, already-referenced unit (research/queue/RQ-20260927-005.yaml, W6-PROP-R3, untouched by this PR), and updates its two sibling units' cross-references to match; files one pipeline finding (PI-20260928-0928CRON-0001) about a research-queue-dispatch cron drift/miss observed via mcp__github__actions_list. Nothing here changes runtime behaviour, order-path code, or any account/strategy config.
